common_name: Blue Ribbons Clematis (Non-Vining Large-Flowered Indigo-Blue Bell Clematis)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in spring in well-drained soil in full sun; this non-climbing clematis forms an upright clump and needs no trellis, though a twiggy support helps keep the lax stems from flopping.

directions: Selected for flowers nearly twice the size of the species, Blue Ribbons bears solitary, widely bell-shaped, deep indigo-blue blooms with gently recurved tepal tips held on slender stems above mounded foliage from midsummer into early fall. As a true integrifolia-type clematis it grows as a self-supporting herbaceous clump rather than a climbing vine, making it equally at home in a perennial border or scrambling through low shrubs. Because flowers form on new growth, cut the whole clump back near ground level in late winter, and divide congested clumps every few years to maintain vigorous bloom.

common_name: Rose Colored Glasses Clematis (Non-Vining Rose-Pink Bell Clematis)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container stock in spring in well-drained, fertile soil in full sun; this clump-forming clematis needs no climbing support and benefits from a light twiggy prop to keep stems upright.

directions: Arising as a seedling selection valued for flowers noticeably larger and deeper in color than the species, Rose Colored Glasses produces nodding, bell-shaped blooms in a rich rose-pink with slightly twisted, recurved tepal tips from early summer through early fall. Like other integrifolia-type clematis it grows as a non-climbing, clumping perennial rather than a true vine, making it a good fit for the middle of a sunny border where it can lean lightly on neighboring plants. Cut the clump back near the ground in late winter since bloom occurs entirely on the current season's growth, and divide every few years to keep the clump from thinning out.

common_name: Little Bas Clematis (Compact Violet-Blue Bell Viticella Clematis)

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring with the crown a couple of inches below the soil surface, keeping roots cool and shaded; Little Bas is a viticella-type clematis that blooms on new growth and can be cut back hard each late winter (Group 3).

directions: A Dutch-raised viticella selection, Little Bas bears small, slightly drooping, violet-blue bells veined with white around a pale throat, opening to reveal a cluster of light stamens against a small green center. It flowers in great numbers from June into September on a more restrained vine than many viticella types, reaching only about ten feet, which suits a smaller obelisk, fence section, or large container. Because it blooms entirely on new growth, cut the whole vine back hard to a low pair of buds each late winter to keep the dense flowering habit.

common_name: Fairy Dance Clematis (Nodding Pink-Purple Viticella Clematis)

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring with the crown a couple of inches below the soil surface, keeping roots cool and shaded; Fairy Dance is a viticella-type clematis that blooms on new growth and can be cut back hard each late winter (Group 3).

directions: A Polish-bred viticella cultivar, Fairy Dance produces nodding, bell-shaped flowers that shift from purple-blue toward pink-purple toward the tepal edges, with noticeably darker veining running through each petal. It flowers prolifically from June until September on a moderately sized climber reaching eight to nine feet, with young stems and foliage carrying a purplish tinge that complements the bloom color. Since flowering occurs entirely on the current season's growth, cut the whole vine back hard in late winter to encourage dense new growth and maximize bloom.

common_name: Fairy Slippers Clematis (Creamy White Bell Viticella Clematis Brushed Pink-Purple)

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring with the crown a couple of inches below the soil surface, keeping roots cool and shaded; Fairy Slippers is a viticella-type clematis that blooms on new growth and can be cut back hard each late winter (Group 3).

directions: Also from Polish viticella breeding, Fairy Slippers bears nodding, bell-shaped flowers that open creamy white at the base and are brushed with soft pink and purple toward the tepal tips, giving a watercolor-like bicolor effect distinct from the solid-colored viticella classics. Blooming from midsummer into early fall on a climber reaching eight to ten feet, it pairs well with darker-flowered viticella cultivars trained on the same support for color contrast. Cut the whole vine back hard to a low pair of buds each late winter, since flowers form only on the current year's growth.

common_name: Carlotta Clematis (Blue Bell-Shaped Viticella Clematis with Red Anthers)

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring with the crown a couple of inches below the soil surface, keeping roots cool and shaded; Carlotta is a viticella-type clematis that blooms on new growth and can be cut back hard each late winter (Group 3).

directions: An English-raised viticella selection, Carlotta bears broadly bell-shaped, pendent blue flowers with four elliptic tepals whose tips recurve slightly as the bloom matures. Inside, violet-purple filaments carry unusually large, deep beetroot-red anthers dusted with white pollen, giving each nodding flower a striking contrast of cool blue and warm red-purple tones. Flowering on new growth from midsummer into early fall, the whole vine can be cut back hard to a low pair of buds each late winter to renew vigor and keep bloom dense.
